observation_summary: The compiler was incorrectly transforming variable declarations, specifically failing to handle duplicate declarations between externs and source code correctly, leading to broken namespace definitions.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved changing the signature of the 'onRedeclaration' method in the 'RedeclarationHandler' interface and updating all implementations to pass a 'CompilerInput' object instead of multiple individual nodes (parent, gramps, etc.). This is a classic interface contract mismatch where the previous signature did not provide enough context (the input source) to correctly determine if a redeclaration was valid (i.e., one in externs, one in source). The change to the interface and the subsequent propagation of the 'CompilerInput' parameter is a structural change to the communication contract between the scope creator and the redeclaration handler.
evidence_used: The fix modifies the 'RedeclarationHandler' interface signature.
The fix adds 'CompilerInput' to the 'onRedeclaration' method signature.
The fix removes redundant parameters (parent, gramps, nodeWithLineNumber) from the interface.
The fix updates 'DuplicateDeclarationHandler' and 'DefaultRedeclarationHandler' to match the new interface.
The fix adds logic to check 'v.isExtern() && !input.isExtern()' inside 'onRedeclaration', which requires the 'CompilerInput' context.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic inside the method was updated, the primary driver for the change was the inability of the existing interface signature to provide the necessary context (CompilerInput) to perform the check, making it an interface/contract issue.
The fix involves changing the communication contract between components (the scope creator and the handler), which is more specific to Interface/O-O Messages than a general relationship issue.
